## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: the guidelines say "Ratio operates a double-blind peer review process", meaning neither author nor reviewer identity is revealed to the other from submission to decision, and authors must anonymise the manuscript and supply a separate title page (live guidelines, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14679329/homepage/forauthors.html, read 2026-11-24; same wording in the 2024-09-22 copy). The live page completes the sentence that was cut off in the archived copy: "Other than in exceptional circumstances", manuscripts are double-blind peer reviewed by a single referee. It also says feedback is provided for all papers that go out for review, and that the final decision rests with the Editor. Survey respondents report an average of 1.0 reviewers per submission (https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/972) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Yes within Wiley: the journal participates in Wiley's Refer and Transfer programme, and a rejected manuscript may be recommended for transfer to another Wiley journal (live guidelines read 2026-11-24; same in the 2024-09-22 copy) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Survey respondents (n=82): initial verdicts 10 acceptances, 51 rejections, 17 revise-and-resubmit and 4 conditional acceptances; of 21 later verdicts, 16 acceptances and 5 rejections (https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/972, all years, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. The live guidelines say only that the final decision on acceptance rests with the Editor (read 2026-11-24); how referee recommendations are used is not stated |

Further journal rules stated in the live guidelines (read 2026-11-24; the 2024-09-22 copy said the same): the editor will not consider more than one submission by the same author at the same time; will not consider a submission from an author who has published in the journal within the previous 18 months (counted between official online publication and the new submission); standard practice is not to correspond with an author whose submission was rejected; and papers by assistant editors or board members are sent to unaffiliated referees (not applicable to the commissioned special issue).

## Format

> Source: the journal's live author guidelines (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14679329/homepage/forauthors.html), read in a real browser on 2026-11-24; the page prints no date. The word limits match the Wayback copy of 2024-09-22.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Three types in the guidelines table: Original Article ("original contribution to new or existing debates or topics", not a discussion piece or reply), Special Issue Article (invited, for the December issue) and Book Review (invited or, occasionally, unsolicited). The guidelines add that the journal seldom publishes discussion pieces, and only on an article published in the journal within the last couple of years |
| **Word limit** | Original Article: 6,000 (minimum) to 7,000 (maximum) words excluding notes and references. Special Issue Article: 7,000 (minimum) to 9,000 (maximum) words excluding notes and references. Book Review: 2,500 words. Measured: median article length 10 pages (quartiles 9 to 12) over 163 of 206 Crossref records with a parseable page range (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0034-0006/works) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The table gives a minimum and a maximum; the live page states no exception procedure (read 2026-11-24) |
| **Abstract limit** | An abstract is required for Original and Special Issue articles (table column "Required"); no length limit is stated on the live page (read 2026-11-24). Measured: abstract median 140 words (quartiles 110 to 166, maximum 209) over 166 Crossref abstracts |
| **Reference limit** | Blank. References and notes are excluded from the word limits above; no separate cap found |
| **Supplementary material** | Figures, supporting information and appendices are supplied as separate files; no size or count limits read |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figures and tables need legends; figure requirements are described by link only |
| **Style / submission format** | Free-format submission: any consistent reference style until acceptance, then an accepted-author style sheet; editable text file (Word, or LaTeX source with a PDF); anonymised main text plus a separate title page; ORCID required; submission through ScholarOne; CrossCheck similarity screening; ethics, data-availability, funding and conflict statements on the title page |

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: Crossref counts over 166 abstracts (regexes in the table); OpenAlex author-country counts over 229 works; the journal's own scope statements (guidelines copy 2024-09-22). Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries of the 229 works in 2021-2026 (OpenAlex works with at least one author in the country; a work can count in several): United Kingdom 51, United States 41, Germany 9, Sweden 8, Switzerland 7, China 7, Netherlands 7, Canada 5, Singapore 5, Italy 4 (https://api.openalex.org/works, filter source S108709262, group_by authorships.countries) |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Rare by count: `\bdecoloni\w*\|\bIndigenous\b\|\bBuddhis\w*\|\bConfuci\w*\|\bDaoi\w*\|\bTaoi\w*\|\bAfrican philosoph\w*\|\bIslamic\b\|\bIndian\b\|\bChinese\b` matches 1 of 166 abstracts (0.6%). The guidelines say the journal "sometimes publishes work from other traditions" while being a journal of analytic philosophy |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Present but small. Feminist, gender or race terms (`\bfeminis\w*\|\bgender\w*\|\bracial\w*\|\brace\b\|\bracis\w*\|\boppress\w*`) 3 of 166 (1.8%); the 2 disability/queer/trans regex hits are "metaphysically queer" in metaethics, not identity topics (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1111/rati.12306). No editorial statement on these topics found |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Analytic, stated by the journal ("Ratio is a journal of analytic philosophy", guidelines copy 2024-09-22). By topic mix: ethics and normative terms 34.3% (57 of 166), epistemology and belief terms 25.9% (43), metaphysics and ontology 15.1% (25), philosophy of science and physics 12.7% (21), logic and formal terms 7.8% (13), history of philosophy (named figures) 7.8% (13). Phenomenology and continental names 1.2% (2). The most cited Crossref items of the window concern AI risk and robot rights (https://doi.org/10.1111/rati.12320, 34 citations; https://doi.org/10.1111/rati.12346, 28). The journal states no political position on any page read |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, several stated by the journal: papers should meet "the highest standards of philosophical expertise" while remaining accessible to readers from a broad range of philosophical areas; the philosophical importance of the issues must be made clear at the start and/or conclusion, and the fact that a topic has been discussed in recent literature is "not, in itself, enough" (guidelines copy 2024-09-22, https://web.archive.org/web/20240922164232/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14679329/homepage/forauthors.html; retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **What kind of engagement?** Free-standing pieces that develop the author's own philosophical perspective are preferred to papers devoted mainly to expounding or criticising others' positions (same copy). Observed practice: 121 of 166 abstracts (72.9%) use argue, defend, thesis or objection language (Crossref).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the guidelines state that highly technical material or reliance on arguments for a narrow specialist audience "will reduce (but not eliminate)" the chances of acceptance, and that a paper not meeting the standard or not appropriate for the journal is returned "without review or feedback" (same copy).
- **Article type and length**: original articles of 6,000 to 7,000 words excluding notes and references; observed median 10 pages (quartiles 9 to 12; https://api.crossref.org/journals/0034-0006/works).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref journal-article records of this journal dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 whose title or abstract matches the regex, over the 166 records with an abstract (81% of 206). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Where I read the hits and they were not uses of the method, the score is set from the hits actually read and the row says so. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 0 | Regex `\bparticipants\b\|\bsurvey\w*\|\bvignette\w*\|\bexperiment[s]? (?:with\|on\|in which)\b` 4 of 166 (2.4%); all 4 were read and none reports participant data. The 1 "quantitative/statistical" hit is a philosophical use |
| Qualitative interviews | 0 | Regex `\bqualitative\b\|\binterview\w*\|\bethnograph\w*\|\bthematic analysis\b` 1 of 166; read, a philosophical use ("qualitative features") |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Regex `\bautoethnograph\w*\|\bethnograph\w*` 0 of 166 |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `\bargue\w*\|\bdefend\w*\|\bthesis\b\|\bobjection\w*` 121 of 166 (72.9%); `\bconceptual\w*\|\banalysis of\b\|\baccount of\b\|\btheory of\b` 48 (28.9%) |
| Formal / logical proof (added row) | 2 | `\btheorem\w*\|\bprove[sd]?\b\|\bproof\w*\|\bformal (?:model\|framework\|semantics\|system)\w*\|\bmodel-theor\w*\|\baxiom\w*` 6 of 166 (3.6%) falls in the 1-5% band (score 2 by the convention); the broader logic/formal pattern is 13 of 166 (7.8%). Score 2 is used |
| Mixed methods | 0 | `\bmixed[- ]method\w*` 0 of 166 |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 0 | `\bsystematic review\w*\|\bmeta-analys\w*\|\bscoping review\w*` 0 of 166 |

| Bioethics, medicine, health | Present | 8 of 166 (4.8%); regex `\bmedical\b\|\bbioethic\w*\|\bhealth\b\|\bdeath\b\|\babortion\b\|\beuthanasia\b\|\bdisease\b` |
| Animals, environment, climate | Rare | 1 of 166 (0.6%) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The guidelines require details of IRB approval, ethical treatment of human and animal participants and informed consent "as appropriate", and a conflict-of-interest declaration on submission (copy 2024-09-22, https://web.archive.org/web/20240922164232/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14679329/homepage/forauthors.html). No participant-data article was found in the abstracts, so the rule is rarely engaged |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are the norm: 159 of 184 Crossref records with an author list (86.4%), 2021-2026 (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0034-0006/works) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The guidelines ask for institutional affiliation where the work was conducted and state no independent-scholar rule; no affiliation data collected beyond countries |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The journal "encourages data sharing" and points to Wiley's data-sharing policy; a data availability statement is listed among the statements on the title page (guidelines copy 2024-09-22) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind review with a separate title page (guidelines copy 2024-09-22). The journal does not accept articles previously published on preprint servers (same copy), so a preprint rules out submission here |
| **AI use** | Disclosure required when AI contributes substantially; AI cannot be an author (https://www.wiley.com/en-us/publish/article/ai-guidelines/), retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; no submission fees; OA APC listed by OpenAlex as USD 2900, unverified against the publisher. 108 of 206 articles carry a Creative Commons licence URL in Crossref |
| **Resubmission limits** | One submission per author at a time, and none from an author published in the journal within the previous 18 months (guidelines copy 2024-09-22) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Prior preprint**: the journal does not accept articles previously published on preprint servers (Preprint Policy, guidelines copy 2024-09-22). A manuscript already on a preprint server is outside the stated rule.
- **Length**: original articles are stated as 6,000 to 7,000 words excluding notes and references (Format); a paper outside that band departs from the stated range, and the guidelines do not say whether exceptions are granted.
- **Repeat submissions**: one paper per author at a time and no submission from an author published in the journal in the previous 18 months (Peer Review, guidelines copy 2024-09-22).
- **Anonymisation**: the manuscript must be anonymised with a separate title page (Format, Peer Review).
- **AI use**: undisclosed substantial AI use or AI-altered evidential images breach the publisher policy (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Audience**: the guidelines say specialist-only or highly technical argument reduces the chances of acceptance, and that the importance of the issue must be stated early or at the end (Framing Requirements).
- **Time**: the stated aim is a decision in two to three months, and the live metrics page gives a 2025 median of 15 days to first decision and 78 days to acceptance; survey respondents average 2.1 months to a response and 7.7 months to publication (Review Cycle Time).
- **Competition**: publisher-reported acceptance rate 22% for 2025 (live metrics page, read 2026-11-24), older 20% (undated); survey respondents report 12.20% of 82 initial verdicts as acceptances (Metrics).
- **Feedback**: papers returned by the editor go back without review or feedback, and the editor does not normally correspond after a rejection (Peer Review).
- **Open access cost**: green deposit of the accepted version is delayed 24 months for humanities and social science journals under the publisher page (Preprint Policy); gold access lists an APC of USD 2900 per OpenAlex, unverified.

### Best Suited For

- Free-standing, argument-driven analytic papers aimed at a general philosophical readership: 72.9% of abstracts use argue, defend, thesis or objection language; ethics (34.3%) and epistemology (25.9%) are the largest topic groups (Orientation, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Short papers: median 10 pages, 9 to 12 quartiles, and a stated 6,000 to 7,000 word band (Format).
- Single-author work: 86.4% of records with an author list are single-author (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Papers already on a preprint server (Preprint Policy; journal's own rule).
- Empirical, participant-based or qualitative studies: none was found in 166 abstracts (Methodological Preferences). The count shows absence, not a stated exclusion.
- Highly technical or narrowly specialist work: the guidelines say it reduces the chances (Framing Requirements); formal-proof terms appear in 3.6% of abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Work centred on non-Western, decolonial or identity topics: non-Western terms 0.6%, gender and race terms 1.8% (Sensitive Topics). A frequency, not a stated exclusion.

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The first row is stated by the journal itself (Refer and Transfer to another Wiley journal); the rows below it are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus (general analytic philosophy), listed only because they share the subject area. No fit evidence was collected for them.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | Another Wiley journal, by editor recommendation | The guidelines say the journal participates in Wiley's Refer and Transfer programme (Peer Review); which journals are offered is not stated |
| 2 | [Philosophical Studies](philosophical-studies.md) | General analytic philosophy; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [Pacific Philosophical Quarterly](pacific-philosophical-quarterly.md) | General analytic philosophy; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
